headline: National Park Entry and Camping Reservations
reservation: Pay the park entrance fee at a visitor center or kiosk. Furnace Creek is the only NPS campground that accepts reservations, for October 15–April 15; reservations are strongly recommended. Other NPS campgrounds operate first come, first served when open. Backcountry camping has separate requirements.

days.title: Salt Flats and Painted Hills

stops.name: Badwater Basin
stops.detail: Walk onto the vast salt flats at the lowest point in North America.

stops.name: Artists Palette
stops.detail: Drive the one-way loop to see volcanic hills colored by mineral oxidation.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for driving and stops; conditions vary with heat
days.note: Avoid walking on salt flats after 10 AM if temperatures are high.

days.title: Canyons and High Overlooks

stops.name: Golden Canyon
stops.detail: Hike through towering yellow cathedral-like walls and mudstone hills.

stops.name: Dante's View
stops.detail: Ascend to the ridge of the Black Mountains for a bird's-eye view of the valley floor.

days.driving: Allow 4 hours total; steep mountain grades to Dante's View
days.note: Dante's View is significantly cooler and windier than the valley floor.

days.title: Sand Dunes and Ghost Towns

stops.name: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes
stops.detail: Explore the shifting sands early in the day to see animal tracks and ripple patterns.

stops.name: Rhyolite Ghost Town
stops.detail: Visit the preserved ruins and art installations just outside the park boundary near Beatty.

days.driving: Allow 3-4 hours; involves crossing the park boundary
days.note: Walking in sand is strenuous; carry double the water you think you need.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Lots at Badwater Basin and Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes are paved but fill during peak winter weekends. Arrive early at Zabriskie Point to ensure a spot for sunrise views.

intel.title: Extreme Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect no cellular service throughout the vast majority of the park, including most canyons and dunes. Emergency satellite devices and offline maps are highly recommended.

intel.title: Remote Pumping
intel.text: Fuel is only available at Furnace Creek, Stovepipe Wells, and Panamint Springs within the park. Prices are typically much higher than in gateway towns like Beatty or Pahrump.

intel.title: Heat Constraints
intel.text: From May through September, outdoor activity is discouraged after mid-morning due to extreme heat. Winter daylight is short, so plan to be off backcountry roads before dark.

intel.title: Flash Flood Road Damage
intel.text: Desert roads are frequently closed for months following seasonal storms due to debris and washouts. Always check the 'Plan Your Visit' section of the NPS website for daily road reports.

plan.arrival: Pickup rental at Las Vegas (LAS) or Boulder City (BLD). Stop in Pahrump for groceries and water before entering the park via Death Valley Junction.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD is essential for backcountry roads like Titus Canyon; check rental terms as many prohibit off-pavement use.
plan.goldenHour: Zabriskie Point; colors change rapidly on the badlands based on the sun's angle and seasonal dust.
